messages.subject: Re: expanding reactiveValues
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex -

Here's a demonstration of the dependencies taken with names():

# Create a reactive values object
v <- reactiveValues(a=1, b=2)

# Add an observer that takes a dependency on v's names, and prints them
# when invalidated (and invalidated objects are flushed)
observe({
  print(names(v))
})

# Flush invalidated objects: prints names(v)
shiny:::flushReact()
# [1] "a" "b"

# No effect on second run; observer wasn't invalidated
shiny:::flushReact()
# <No output>

# Change value of a: observer isn't invalidated
v$a <- 2
shiny:::flushReact()
# <No output>

# Add a new object; observer is invalidated
v$c <- 3
shiny:::flushReact()
# [1] "a" "b" "c"

-Winston

Yes, although depending on how long it takes to "suck in new data", you might not want to have the data fetching happen in the Shiny process itself, as the data fetching will block the app from doing anything else. If it'll take a long time then you could just set up a separate R script for downloading the data to disk, and run it automatically using cron or something similar.

If you do want to run it in Shiny, then you would do it by setting up a reactive expression that does the querying and returns a data frame, and also calls invalidateLater with however long you want between refreshes.

I then resigned in and when I tried to open my shiny app code, I got the error that while opening there was no such file or directory. The glimmer website gives an error of the application failed to start. Any help is much appreciated.

messages.body_plain:
Joe,

Thanks again.

OK, so here's what I did:

1) To make sure that there's no "legacy configuration" issues, I started with a fresh install of Ubuntu13.04
2) Install R, shiny, nodejs and shiny-serve according to install procedures on shiny-server website
3) copy examples folder to shiny-server/www folder
4) launch shiny server
5) successively run and close several of the applications in the examples folder
6) in xterm, type: ps aux  so as to see the details of all processes running.

As you continue to run and then close the browser windows, I'm seeing (via ps aux)  that there's a growing list of shiny processes persisting. Closing the browser or shutting down shiny-server has no effect---the only way to stop the multiple shiny processes is to manually kill them.

Is this what you are seeing as well?

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: grid.locator() in shiny webapp?
messages.body_plain:
Prompted by Susan and Yihui, I decided to take a quick look at this and found the R graphics devices to be much simpler than I had expected!

Here's a proposed implementation:

devtools::install_github("shiny", "jcheng5", ref="plot-mouse-events")

This adds two new parameters to plotOutput: clickId and hoverId. If you provide names for them, they will start providing reactive values under those names in the usual way. The values will have x and y (or the whole value may be NULL if the plot has never been clicked, or the plot is not currently being hovered over). And importantly, the x and y values will be in user coordinates, not pixels!

Example:
https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269
shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269")

The main thing I know doesn't work right now (at least it shouldn't) is that you will get funky results on Retina displays. It should be a straightforward fix.

Also, I know it doesn't work on ggplot2 plots (though locator() doesn't work on ggplot2 either).

Please try it and let us know if it works, especially on funkier graphs. If you find any graphs where locator() works but this doesn't, let us know!

I don't see this problem normally but there have been times when we've had extra R processes hanging around seemingly forever, so I don't doubt what you're seeing. messages.subject_clean: Default value for input generated by reactiveUI
messages.body_plain:
when storing certain objects in a reactiveValue, dependence on the identical function may lead to excessive computation.... not terribly difficult to work around, but it may explain some cases where the UI seems to hang up. cheers!

> library(xcms)
> library(faahKO)
> cdfpath <- system.file('cdf',package='faahKO')
> cdffiles <- list.files(cdfpath,recursive=TRUE,full.names=TRUE)
> raw1 <- xcmsRaw(cdffiles[1])
> raw2 <- xcmsRaw(cdffiles[1])
> identical(raw1, raw2)
[1] FALSE
> identical(xcmsRaw(cdffiles[1]), xcmsRaw(cdffiles[1]))
[1] FALSE
>
> all.equal(raw1, raw2)
[1] TRUE

On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 10:02 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> We are doing exact equality testing, my understanding is identical is the most appropriate function for that.
>
>

> > > On Fri, Dec 14, 2012 at 9:01 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > > Actually this is because of a mistake in my randomList implementation, I think if you change 0 to "0" the problem will go away. By reading randomList instead of input$randomList, you're insulated from the changes in input$randomList. When randomList recalculates, if the new value is the same as the previous value, no changes are propagated.
> > > >
> > > >

> > > > > [1] "output$nullOutput func depends on input$randomList - value = 0"

> > > > > >   if (is.null(input$randomList))
> > > > > >     0
> > > > > >   else

On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 7:55 PM, Susan Vander Plas <srvand...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Joe, you just made my night. This will make my life a LOT easier.
>
>
> On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 7:51 PM, Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > This is so awesome! Now I can smell a lot of interesting interactive
> > graphics applications approaching. We, just, need, this, right, now!
> > :)
> >
> > It will be even more awesome if mousedown/mouseup events can
> > supported. Then we will be able to select elements in a region, and
> > that is an important step to interactive graphics. But it actually
> > suffices to have click and hover only, e.g. we can click twice to
> > define a region. It is just a matter of user experience.
> >
> > Regards,
> > Yihui
> > --
> > Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
> > Phone: 206-667-4385 Web: http://yihui.name
> > Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Seattle
> >
> >
> > On Fri, Jun 21, 2013 at 5:21 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > Prompted by Susan and Yihui, I decided to take a quick look at this and
> > > found the R graphics devices to be much simpler than I had expected!
> > >
> > > Here's a proposed implementation:
> > >
> > > devtools::install_github("shiny", "jcheng5", ref="plot-mouse-events")
> > >
> > > This adds two new parameters to plotOutput: clickId and hoverId. If you
> > > provide names for them, they will start providing reactive values under
> > > those names in the usual way. The values will have x and y (or the whole
> > > value may be NULL if the plot has never been clicked, or the plot is not
> > > currently being hovered over). And importantly, the x and y values will be
> > > in user coordinates, not pixels!
> > >
> > > Example:
> > > https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269
> > > shiny::runGist("https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/5835269")
> > >
> > > The main thing I know doesn't work right now (at least it shouldn't) is that
> > > you will get funky results on Retina displays. It should be a
> > > straightforward fix.
> > >
> > > Also, I know it doesn't work on ggplot2 plots (though locator() doesn't work
> > > on ggplot2 either).
> > >
> > > Please try it and let us know if it works, especially on funkier graphs. If
> > > you find any graphs where locator() works but this doesn't, let us know!
> > >
> > >
> > >

> > >>

> > >> Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Seattle

messages.subject: Feedback on Tennis Simulation App
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone! I just finished making my first webapp with Shiny, and first webapp ever. Here's the link <http://spark.rstudio.com/ccagrawal/tennis-sim/>. It uses Highcharts, and I used Winston Chang's dashboard app <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winstontest/shiny-jsdemo/> to help me out.

Basically, you input a probability of winning individual points, and the app simulates tennis matches and outputs the percentage of points, games, tiebreakers, sets, and matches that are won. It's really interesting to see how small of a point advantage you need to basically guarantee winning the match.

I hope to eventually use rCharts; I just wasn't sure if rCharts had the ability to dynamically update charts. Does anybody have any suggestions or comments?

messages.subject: Shiny app with googleVis - 2012 best cities of US- some questions
messages.subject_clean: Shiny app with googleVis - 2012 best cities of US- some questions
messages.body_plain:
In putting together my first shiny app with googleVis (discussed at http://analyticsandvisualization.blogspot.com/2013/06/revisualizing-best-cities-in-us-in-2012.html), I had three questions regarding googleVis, which Markus Gesmann answered. In that application, I used a motion chart to show scatter plots. Those questions might be of interest to some in this group.They were regarding google chart tools, as Markus explained. I would appreciate any inputs on how these issues can be addressed using alternate tools.

1. In GeoChart: In my data, I have a variable with a paragraph of  10 lines, say, to describe each country studied. I tried to use that as my hover variable, but there was a truncation of what was shown and it all came in just one line. Is this a limitation of the functionality for now?
Markus: Indeed, I believe this is a current limitation.

2. In motion chart: example could be the Fruit data in the googleVis package. If we did a basic plot(gvisMotionChart(Fruits, "Fruit", "Year")), the output provides the ability to modify the horizontal axis to sales, profit, expenses, time and the vertical axis provides the ability to Expenses, Profit and Sales. Is it possible to provide only a subset of these vars and not all default vars? For example, could I provide only profit and expenses for horizontal axis, and sales and expenses for vertical axis? Other options being the same (for color, size, etc.)
Markus: No, I am afraid this is not possible.

3. Can I size a bubble based on a variable such that a lower value indicated bigger size? I was able to create a reordered variable, but two problems it created were (a) the hover value for size was the modified value and not the original value, and (b) this newly created variable was also available as an option for the horizontal and vertical axis, taking us back to question 2 above.
Markus: I don't think so either

Thanks,
Vivek

messages.body_plain:
Hi Giles,

I'm not sure how much time Winston plans to expend maintaining shiny-gridster, but I expect he'll be able to chime in on that.

As one alternative, I've been working on ShinyDash (https://github.com/trestletech/ShinyDash), which was initially a fork of Winston's shiny-gridster work. It's basically a rewrite of Winston's initial prototyping but uses Rickshaw instead of HighCharts (to maintain MIT licensing) and then adds a few new widgets/extensions. You can see an example here: http://spark.rstudio.com/trestletech/ShinyDash-Sample/

I'll let the other authors speak to the plans of their Shiny Gridster packages, but I do plan to continue development on this package and maintain it. Ultimately, we'll be releasing it on CRAN once it's stable.

Jeff

messages.body_plain:
Another package making use of gridster, and built on top of Winston's ideas is dashifyr.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ramnathv/dashifyr

Dashifyr integrates seamlessly with rCharts, which provides access to multiple JS charting libraries, including Highchart and Polycharts. By design rCharts exposes the complete API of the charting libraries, implying that any chart you can create in JS, you can create using rCharts, and hence include in dashifyr.

I do plan to release it on CRAN, but it might take a bit longer, since I need to put rCharts on CRAN first. However, a stable version will be maintained on github and questions addressed.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Ramnath

I did look at the code, and did not see your use of local({}), as in Winston's example, which I believe may be the crux of the issue, after replacing the plot functions with the appropriate table generation functions.

  # Call renderPlot for each one. Plots are only actually generated when they
  # are visible on the web page.
  for (i in 1:max_plots) {
    # Need local so that each item gets its own number. Without it, the value
    # of i in the renderPlot() will be the same across all instances, because
    # of when the expression is evaluated.
    local({
      my_i <- i
      plotname <- paste("plot", my_i, sep="")

      output[[plotname]] <- renderPlot({
        plot(1:my_i, 1:my_i,
             xlim = c(1, max_plots),
             ylim = c(1, max_plots),
             main = paste("1:", my_i, ".  n is ", input$n, sep = "")
        )
      })
    })
  }

messages.body_plain: Andrew, The trouble is that renderTable uses xtable which by default sanitizes the output, like escaping HTML. Here is an Rmd file that shows how you can prevent this. The key is to specify a sanitize.text.function that does not escape anything. You can tweak it so that only the flags column is not escaped. Shiny does allow you to pass options to xtable in renderTable. So you should be able to use this idea to display your flags as images. Hope this helps. Cheers, Ramnath ## Test ```{r results = 'asis', comment = NA} require(xtable) options(xtable.type = 'html') dat <- data.frame( country = c('USA', 'China'), flag = c('', '') ) print(xtable(dat), sanitize.text.function = function(x) x) ``` On Monday, June 24, 2013 2:47:55 PM UTC-4, Andrew Clark wrote: > Thanks for taking time out. shinyServer(function(input, output) {

messages.body_plain:
Here is the idea. You create a makefile in the root directory of your application on your local machine with the following code. Make sure to substitute username, repo and local-repo (which will most likely be the current directory if you are already inside your app).

If you now run make deploy in the command line, it will both push your repo to github AND to glimmer.

deploy:
   git push g...@github.com:<username>/<repo>
   rsync -avz --delete <local-repo> <username>@glimmer.rstudio.com:~/ShinyApps/

messages.body_plain:
This works fine for me (requires Shiny 0.6.0 to run Shiny apps inline like this; adapting to server.r and ui.r is straightforward):

runApp(list(
  server = function(input, output, session) {
    makePlot <- function() {
      plot(1:input$n, 1:input$n)
    }

    output$myPlot <- renderPlot({
      makePlot()
    }, height=400, width=800)

    output$downloadPlot <- downloadHandler(
      filename = function() {

        'report.pdf'

      },
      content = function(file) {
        pdf(file, onefile=T, width=8.5, height=11)

        makePlot()
        dev.off()
      },
      contentType = 'application/pdf'
    )
  },

  ui = pageWithSidebar(
      headerPanel('Downloading Data'),
      sidebarPanel(
        sliderInput("n", "Number of points:", min = 1, max = 50, value = 10),
        downloadButton('downloadPlot', 'Download')
      ),
      mainPanel(
        plotOutput("myPlot")
      )
    )
  )
)

messages.subject: Re: Shiny and 'raster' Package: Plotting issues
messages.body_plain:
It looks like your selectInput is associating "Map1" with a raster object (the output of raster()). I'm not familiar with the package, but I'm guessing this is not a string. The items in the selectInput should all be character strings, perhaps something like this:

 selectInput("variable", "Map",

                list("Map1" = "Map1",
                     "Map2" = "Map2"))

And then on the server side, you can fetch the appropriate object:
 output$mapPlot <- renderPlot({
    if (input$variable == "Map1")
      data <- raster("file1.asc")
    else if (input$variable == "Map2")
      data <- raster("file2.asc")

    levelplot(data, margin=FALSE, par.settings=GrTheme)
  })

BTW, the reason I use an if-else statement, instead of doing something like this:
  data <- raster(input$variable)
is because this would allow users to potentially read any file on your system, by simply modifying the input value in the web browser.

-Winston

messages.subject_clean: Duplicate binding error when renaming tab
messages.body_plain:
I have a tabSet generator that's generated UI.

When I replace the tabSet generator (by re-running the UI) and one of the tabs IDs changes, I get a duplicate binding error for an output contained in the replacement tab.

This shouldn't happen because the old tab is going away as part of the update.

The effect of this is that the tab set no longer operates correctly - it doesn't supply updated input values for the tab bar itself.

-Alex

messages.subject: Re: Duplicate binding error when renaming tab
messages.subject_clean: Duplicate binding error when renaming tab
messages.body_plain:
Looks like the first visit to the duplicated htmloutput is in a recursed call to bindouputs, the second is from the original call:

attached image showing the first.

When rebinding outputs, ALL outputs from the scope are considered, even if nested in other htmloutputs.

Bindoutput does this test:

      if (this.$values[id] !== undefined)
        binding.onValueChange(this.$values[id]);

Which means child htmloutputs of the current binding are bound now, even though they are still in the queue for binding from the original call.

When the original call considers them, they already appear to be bound, which causes a fault, and stops consideration of further bindings, and does not send the updated inputs back to the server.

-Alex

On Tuesday, June 25, 2013 1:56:24 PM UTC-7, Alex Brown wrote:
> I have a tabSet generator that's generated UI.
>
> When I replace the tabSet generator (by re-running the UI) and one of the tabs IDs changes, I get a duplicate binding error for an output contained in the replacement tab.
>
> This shouldn't happen because the old tab is going away as part of the update.
>
> The effect of this is that the tab set no longer operates correctly - it doesn't supply updated input values for the tab bar itself.
>
> -Alex

> > Looks like the first visit to the duplicated htmloutput is in a recursed call to bindouputs, the second is from the original call:
> >
> > attached image showing the first.
> >
> > When rebinding outputs, ALL outputs from the scope are considered, even if nested in other htmloutputs.
> >
> > Bindoutput does this test:
> >
> >       if (this.$values[id] !== undefined)
> >         binding.onValueChange(this.$values[id]);
> >
> > Which means child htmloutputs of the current binding are bound now, even though they are still in the queue for binding from the original call.
> >
> > When the original call considers them, they already appear to be bound, which causes a fault, and stops consideration of further bindings, and does not send the updated inputs back to the server.

> It looks like your selectInput is associating "Map1" with a raster object (the output of raster()). I'm not familiar with the package, but I'm guessing this is not a string. The items in the selectInput should all be character strings, perhaps something like this:
>  selectInput("variable", "Map",
>                 list("Map1" = "Map1",
>                      "Map2" = "Map2"))
>
>
> And then on the server side, you can fetch the appropriate object:
>  output$mapPlot <- renderPlot({
>     if (input$variable == "Map1")
>       data <- raster("file1.asc")
>     else if (input$variable == "Map2")
>       data <- raster("file2.asc")
>
>     levelplot(data, margin=FALSE, par.settings=GrTheme)
>   })
>
>
> BTW, the reason I use an if-else statement, instead of doing something like this:
>   data <- raster(input$variable)
> is because this would allow users to potentially read any file on your system, by simply modifying the input value in the web browser.

> -Winston

messages.subject: Re: Inline twitter js?
messages.body_plain:
You can use tags$head with tags$script to include JS files. For example, here's some code from dateInput, which includes a Javascript and CSS file:

  singleton(tags$head(
    tags$script(src = "shared/datepicker/js/bootstrap-datepicker.min.js"),
    tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", type = "text/css",
              href = 'shared/datepicker/css/datepicker.css')
  ))

The singleton() wrapper function tells it not to include the contents more than once in a page.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: memory management
messages.body_plain:
Does it happen only after you've run it a number of times? If so, it may be that your code is using memory and not freeing it up, due to references to old unused objects.

Also, what kind of instance are you running on? The micro instances only have about 600MB of memory, and typically aren't configured to use virtual memory (which would be costly and slow on EBS).

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: shiny error help!
messages.body_plain:
input$var is a string in this case, so you're effectively doing something like this:
  boxplot("x1")

I think you want to do this:
  boxplot(x1)

And to do that, you need to get the variable (using global env here, but you may want something different:
  get(input$var, envir = .GlobalEnv)

However, if your app will be publicly accessible, it's probably not a good idea to simply grab whatever variable the client asks for, because it's very easy for someone to simply change the input variable to anything, and they could potentially view almost anything in memory of your R process. You can avoid this by using if statmeents -  see here:
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/fe5kE6SUfM0/oceXTO41Q0UJ

okay, it's very useful to wrap these functions up, since I can see using poll, certainly.

In general I'm now feeling it would be great to get some of the more profound use cases wrapped up in a standard or example implementation - coordinating writes to a single file or database for multi-user interaction with a core dataset seems pretty important and I'm no idea how it might work in the reactive model.  I'm prepared to be astonished by how elegant it tuns out to be, but right now I'm guessing.

The solutions above do polling, and I'm looking in another direction at the moment - I want to build asynchrony into shiny by allowing it to spawn jobs using R parallel and system fork/exec, and then get the results back in the following ways:

  a reactive that triggers when it gets the signal that the child has finished.  Using ... wait?
  a reactive that triggers when a file gets updated (for larger results or ones where R would have to write it back to the FS first anyway (e.g. images)  using select()
  a side reactive that monitors stderr to read progress from long running jobs.  Using select()

-Alex

messages.subject: Local names for inputs, outputs
messages.body_plain:
I'm building list + detail views in shiny, and right now I'm bumping into problems of state leaking in between the data from different records.

Part of this is due to the 'asynchronous' parallel nature of shiny reactives, perhaps I'm using it wrong:

  If my record view contains both first level outputs and outputs inside renderOutputs, then the outputs are updated first, then the render output runs and the inner outputs are executed.  If this takes a long time, the 'name' of the user may be displayed long before the 'photo' (inside a render output) is updated, since that needs a round trip to the client to cause it to be updated.

Part of this is due to a js throw that I'm hitting due to a false detection of duplicate names in a nested hierarchy of renderOutputs

Part of this is due to the lack (in HTML #id and shiny names) for local names for things:

For example, if I have a database with 10 rows, and I want to select a row and display the record, the very same ui widgets and output$s are used for one record and the next.

Imagine if html id's were local and nested - I would simply need to set an id for the record view container, and the inner inputs and outputs would get local names that could not be confused with those from the previous record.

I'm not sure how nesting would work on the shiny side - perhaps nested 'server' objects.

Please help!

-Alex

messages.subject: Shiny fileInput 'raster' Package ASCII
messages.body_plain:
Hey,

I would like to use the file upload controls fileInput in R shiny to import an ASCII file using rasterfrom the raster Package, do some math with the imported raster layer and plot it in the end. When I try this, I get the following error:
>
> Error in .local(x, ...) : list has no "x"

Is there a way to get ASCII files imported as raster with the R shiny file upload controls? As I don't know how to create a ASCII file within R, you can download one here <https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/17914446/example.asc> to make the example reproducible.

ui.R
library(shiny)
library(raster)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

headerPanel("Header1"),

sidebarPanel(
fileInput('layer', 'Choose Layer', multiple=FALSE, accept='asc')
),

mainPanel(
plotOutput("mapPlot")
)
))

server.R
library(shiny)
library(raster)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$mapPlot <- renderPlot({

inFile <- input$layer

if (is.null(inFile))
  return(NULL)

data <- raster(inFile)

plot(data)

})
})

Thank you very much!

Viktor

messages.body_plain:
actionButton works multiple times. You use it like this:

observe({
  if (input$myActionButton == 0)
    return()
  isolate({
    # Run your code here
  })
})

Or like this:

output$myPlot <- renderPlot({
  if (input$myActionButton == 0)
    return(NULL)
  isolate({
    # Do your plotting here
  })
})

The hardest thing will be figuring out how to add additional tabs at runtime. The tabsetPanel control that comes out-of-the-box with Shiny doesn't currently support adding tabs at runtime. You would have to either extend the existing tabsetPanel control using JavaScript, or write your own.

               radioButtons("dist",  "Endpoint type", c("User defined" = "User", "Binomial" = "Binomial")),
               tabsetPanel(
                 tabPanel("User",
                          numericInput(inputId="nfix",label="N for Fixed Design", value=1, min=1)),
                 tabPanel("Binomial",
                          numericInput(inputId="p1",label="Control event rate", value=.15, min=.005,max=.995),
                          numericInput(inputId="p2",label="Experimental event rate", value=.1, min=.005,max=.995),

      switch(input$dist,

        "Binomial" = nBinomial(p1=input$p1,p2=input$p2,delta0=input$delta0,alpha=input$alpha,beta=1-input$Power)
  )})

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server, Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server on Linux, and RODBC problem
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server, Microsoft ODBC Driver for SQL Server on Linux, and RODBC problem
messages.body_plain:
In response to the OP: you have most likely not set up your odbc.ini properly. See below. I add further details because you may also have a unixodbc version issue (it must be 2.3) - but you did not specify.

The MS ODBC drivers have just been updated to version 11 (quite a jump from 1.0, but there it is). Installing it on Ubuntu works if you take the pointers from Andrew K <http://onefinepub.com/2013/03/07/ms-sql-odbc-ubuntu/> into account. Between that post and the Microsoft documentation all steps are well described. I will summarize my steps below for Ubuntu 12.04:

Download from msdn <http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/hh568451%28v=SQL.110%29.aspx> and untar : msodbcsql-11.0.2270.0.tar.gz

Make sure you have all dependencies installed: sudo apt-get install libssl1.0.0 libkrb5-3 glibc-2.13-1 e2fsprogs openssl libkrb5-3

Also check that you have wget (sudo apt-get install wget).

To update you unixodbc version (through the repositories you will have an older version installed) run the command as sudo bash build_dm.sh. I have no clue why it does not seem to work with the ./ prefix, for some reason I need to give the full reference to bash. The installer gives further instructions to make install unixodbc 2.3.

Now install the actual driver: sudo bash install.sh install --accept-license --force

the --force flag is important because otherwise it will complain that there is no rpm installed on the system (which there is not on Ubuntu). This was a tip from Andrew K again.

The installer updated the /etc/odbcinst.ini file to include the driver like so it should now include:

[ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server]
Description=Microsoft ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server
Driver=/opt/microsoft/msodbcsql/lib64/libmsodbcsql-11.0.so.2270.0
Threading=1
UsageCount=2

Seeing this is a check that installation went through correctly.

Now another tip from onefinepub <http://onefinepub.com/2013/03/07/ms-sql-odbc-ubuntu/> is required otherwise it will not work:
sudo ln -s /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcrypto.so.1.0.0 /usr/lib/libcrypto.so.10
sudo ln -s /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.1.0.0 /usr/lib/libssl.so.10

Now make sure that you configure you odbc.ini to make a DSN that connects using the new driver. It will contain the following:

[ConnectionName]
Driver       = ODBC Driver 11 for SQL Server
Description  = ODBC connection to MSSQL Database via the Microsoft Driver
Trace        = No
Server       = xxx
Servername   = xxxx
Database     = xxx
Trace           = No

But it will not contain a username and password. You will have to pass that through to the database server when making the connection (see this post <http://social.technet.microsoft.com/Forums/sqlserver/en-US/d4eab3b3-6254-4644-a1e4-e6866f7507fd/uid-in-odbcini>).

Having done all this your R will look like:

> library(RODBC)
> sqlconnection <- odbcConnect(dsn="DBNAME", uid="UserName", pwd="Pass")

And your connection should be open.

messages.subject: Help with controlling selectInput
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a selectInput control, and I'm trying to add "Previous" and "Next" buttons to the UI that would allow users to cycle through the 122 choices one-by-one... The following code seems to accomplish this functionality, but it's a little bit touchy---like if I push the "Previous" button a few times really quickly, it will start oscillating back and forth between a few different choices and becomes unresponsive. Is there a better way to code this?

Also, I'd like for the app to select a random choice to show on start-up. Right now, when the app loads, it shows choice "121" every time, and I can't figure out why.

Anyway, the relevant portion of the code looks like this:

ui.R:
  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("dropdown"),
    actionButton("dec", label="Previous"),
    actionButton("inc", label="Next")
  )

server.R:
x <- 1:122
names(x) <- as.character(x)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  ### REACTIVE VALUES ###
  values <- reactiveValues(q.num=sample.int <http://sample.int>(122, size=1))

  ### QUESTION SELECTION ###
  # Drop-down
  observe({
    input$q.select
    isolate(values$q.num <- as.numeric(input$q.select))
  })
  # Increment
  observe({
    input$inc
    isolate(values$q.num <- min(122, values$q.num + 1))
  })
  # Decrement
  observe({
    input$dec
    isolate(values$q.num <- max(1, values$q.num - 1))
  })
  # UI Output
  output$dropdown <- renderUI({
    selectInput("q.select", label="Number:", choices=x,
                selected=names(x)[values$q.num])
  })
})

Thoughts?

-- Josh

messages.subject: Re: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?
messages.subject_clean: How can one action trigger two UI changes, one instant, and one waiting for computation to finish?
messages.body_plain:
It's true that outputs hold themselves until all of them are ready. But the same does not apply to session$sendCustomMessage. You can set up an observer that sets the spinning wheel via sendCustomMessage, and give it a higher priority, like so:

progressObserver <- observe({
  input$button
  isolate({
    session$sendCustomMessage("progress", ...)
  })
})
progressObserver$setPriority(10)

This will ensure that the custom message will be sent before executing any other observers that are scheduled at the same time.

The actual implementation of the spinning wheel has to be done in JavaScript, we don't have that as a component yet.
